name: Gold Bar vibrating tool

card.summary: A T-shaped, gold-plated handheld vibrating bar that is glided over the face to smooth, de-puff and contour the look of skin.
card.aka: Gold Bar; Gold Sculpting Bar; 24K gold beauty bar
card.note: Benefit claims come mainly from brands; independent trials of this specific tool are not available.

quick.overview:
The Gold Bar is a battery-powered, T-shaped facial massage tool plated in 24-karat gold. Its short head is pressed to the skin and glided around the eyes, forehead, lips and jawline, and its vibration is marketed as smoothing fine lines, depuffing and giving a lifted look.

Versions sold under the Gold Bar name include a makeup-artist-designed bar from Jillian Dempsey and one from Spa Sciences, along with many generic lookalikes. Any visible effect is usually described as temporary, comparable to facial massage generally.
quick.how: Brands suggest switching the bar on and gliding it with light pressure in upward and outward strokes across the forehead, under the eyes, around the lips and along the jaw, for a few minutes a day over cleansed skin or a serum. Makeup artists use it before makeup to depuff.
quick.risks: Vibrating facial tools are generally low-risk; gentle pressure and a clean surface are the usual label advice. Users with skin conditions, recent procedures or implants typically check with a clinician, and metal-plating allergies are possible.

lead: The Gold Bar is a T-shaped, hand-held vibrating facial tool, usually plated in 24-karat gold over a metal body. The short crossbar fits into contours around the eyes, brow and lips, and users glide it over the face in upward and outward strokes to depuff, smooth and add a lifted look.

Versions sold under the Gold Bar name include one designed by makeup artist Jillian Dempsey and one by Spa Sciences, and many generic gold 'beauty bars' copy the shape. A retailer listing for the Dempsey bar describes a 24K gold-plated bar vibrating at 6,000 vibrations per minute, sourced from Japan, priced at $195, and says it helps depuff, lift and contour and supports circulation and lymphatic drainage.[1] These claims come from the seller.
No published clinical study of this specific tool is known; research exists on facial massage and vibration more generally.

chain: Massage-like motion moves fluid and boosts temporary circulation
angle.text: People use the bar as a quick massage step in a skincare or makeup routine, expecting a temporary depuffed and smoother look. Effects are comparable to other facial massage tools and are described as short-lived.

paras: The tool consists of a vertical handle with a flat crossbar head, plated in gold and powered by a battery that vibrates the bar. Sellers describe the T-shape as suited to fitting the eye area, lips and brow. Retailer copy for the Dempsey version says it relaxes facial muscles through vibration and is not for use in the bath or shower.[1]

sections.h: Use in looksmaxxing and beauty routines
paras: The Dempsey instructions begin with clean skin and a pea-sized amount of moisturizer. The bar is pushed from the jawline up toward the temples along the cheekbones, then from the jawline toward the neck and under the chin, about five minutes per area, without pressing down; the neck lines are treated with vertical glides.[1] Makeup artists use such bars to reduce morning puffiness before applying makeup.
